channel.title: Via Fidelitatis — Faithful FI for Catholic Families
channel.description: Practical financial independence tools and faith-filled stewardship insights for Catholic families. FI calculator, college planning, and generational wealth rooted in fidelity.

item.title: Pay the Debt of Justice: Lessons from St. Gregory the Great
item.description: Gregory sold the family estates and founded monasteries. Surplus left in checking is already owed — when we meet the needy we pay a debt of justice, not offer a gift.

item.title: Give the Windfall a Job: Lessons from St. Ingrid
item.description: A raise sits in checking, then becomes a nicer kitchen. Give the windfall a job first — give, buffer, invest — the way St. Ingrid gave her fortune a vocation.

item.title: Purchasing Is a Moral Act: Lessons from Creation Day
item.description: Most budgets treat “we can afford it” as permission. Naming “enough” makes the purchase a moral act and frees surplus for the poor and the vocation.

item.title: Give Away the Horse: Lessons from St. Aidan
item.description: St. Aidan gave away the king’s horse the same day he received it. Raises and extras are for mercy, not a heavier life.

item.title: He Must Increase: Lessons from St. John the Baptist
item.description: He must increase; we must decrease. Shrink the lifestyle, not the vocation, so there is room to tell the truth and share the surplus.

item.title: Order Your Loves: Lessons from St. Augustine
item.description: God first, enough for the house, the rest for others. Ordered love is the budget — Augustine’s ordo amoris at the kitchen table.

item.title: Stay the Course: Lessons from St. Monica
item.description: Monica prayed for years before Augustine turned. Stay in the budget when the fruit is slow; faithful FI is a long game, not a streak.

item.title: Form Children, Not Status: Lessons from St. Joseph Calasanz
item.description: School costs can be formation or a bumper sticker. Fund the child St. Joseph Calasanz would recognize — piety and letters, not prestige.

item.title: Build Margin for True Justice: Lessons from St. Louis
item.description: A king who washed the feet of the poor. Keep enough slack in the plan that justice is a Tuesday habit, not a heroic weekend.
